correctness.rationale: Primitive square-zero matrices over a finite chain ring are conjugate to the two-by-two Jordan block using a unimodular basis; orbit–stabilizer gives the exact primitive count. Exhaustive matrix-product checker matches every tested field/ring and valuation.

originality.rationale: The inspected decomposition theorem (arXiv:2102.10460v1), all-nilpotent census (DOI:10.1080/03081087.2017.1418826), and trace-zero image-size census (arXiv:1709.02717) do not logically imply the full square-zero valuation profile over arbitrary finite commutative chain rings. The inaccessible Ramirez–Bollman 1969 source leaves a genuine bounded risk of equivalent special cases.

value.rationale: The square-zero locus is a natural index-two stratum in finite matrix rings, directly connected to finite-ring matrix decompositions. The theorem simultaneously determines its size at every nilpotent length and at every entrywise valuation, proves a nonobvious equidistribution across all lower valuations and universality across equal/mixed characteristic chain rings with the same q and n, and packages all lengths in a rational generating function. These are mathematically motivated refinements not forced by prior total-nilpotent counts.
